answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using transitive credit graphs in a peer meadow. Agents must secure bonded vouches from existing nodes, climbing a trust terrace that limits unverified bandwidth. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locking forfeited collateral per identity to forge trust paths. Abnormal query bursts trigger a fee spiral that rapidly drains attacker liquidity. However, this design penalizes legitimate new agents that lack established network ties.
